item.title: [infoq] 向量数据库要被取代？DynamoDB 开始原生支持 AI 搜索
item.description: DynamoDB now has native vector search: embeddings and application data can live in the same table, and developers query them via the SearchVectors API for approximate nearest neighbors, eliminating a separate vector database. It scales serverlessly, supports up to 4,096 dimensions and several distance functions, and can reach trillions of vectors with single-digit-millisecond latency; costs are metered for index writes, queries, and storage.

item.description: Amazon has open-sourced Dogwood, a policy language for AI-agent tool calls that can read an agent’s event history and express temporal constraints, complementing the stateless Cedar. It adds operators such as formerly and sum_within for sequence-level rules, and demonstrates a classic pitfall where rate limits on responses are bypassed by concurrent transfers. A good fit for teams building deterministic guardrails around agent tools.

item.title: [infoq] PostgreSQL 太难懂？有人把它做成了城市模拟器
item.description: Nikolay Samokhvalov released PGSimCity, an open-source educational tool that turns PostgreSQL cluster internals into an interactive 3D city simulation running entirely in the browser. It maps PG 18 components like shared_buffers, WAL, checkpointer, and autovacuum to city districts, letting users trace query execution and trigger failure modes such as sort spills or buffer-eviction contention. Aimed at backend developers, SREs, and DBAs, it bridges the gap between SQL and kernel internals.

item.title: [infoq] Netflix 开源了一个用于因果推理的智能代理工作流
item.description: Netflix open-sourced an agentic workflow for observational causal inference (OCI) that pairs an execution agent with a reviewer agent. The execution agent handles repetitive work such as sensitivity analysis, while humans set the analysis plan and judge results. On ACIC competition data the workflow was competitive; in a game-retention case study, its effect estimate was 25% of a Claude simple-linear-regression baseline, and the reviewer flagged early-adopter bias and a failed placebo test.
